name: The Chess of Fate
aspect: The endless game whose board is the world and whose pieces are its islands, ranges and plates
notes: The primordial cosmic board game played by Indra and Varuṇa, refereed by the Sky Father Dyauṣ Pitar, which shapes the physical and spiritual geography of the Tethys-rim world. Dyauṣ Pitar's sixty-four celestial coordinates are the grid the Harappan sages later revered -- and the same abstract 0-100 grid canon draws its atlas on, which is the joke the myth is telling. Mortals keep rediscovering refractions of the rules: the Jharwa and Tushara bone tallies, and the Mask of Vaṛkesh on its altar at the Sun Plateau, which folds a battle into a tabletop and seats the fighters across a board from the Mask itself.
